title: That’s Why I Did It
author: Ash Wright
summary: Ash Wright begins with a small habit he noticed after moving to a new city: when he realises he is walking the wrong way, he pulls out his phone and pretends a message changed his plans, as though passers-by needed an explanation. He uses the habit to examine how leaders over-explain a change of direction, using the example of a team update process that someone suggests replacing with a shared report. He links the urge to justify an earlier decision to escalation of commitment, where people keep investing in an inferior approach. His conclusion is that committing to a plan does not oblige anyone to defend it once something better appears. The real cost, he argues, is the time spent defending the original position, and he resolves to correct course without apologies or explanations.
points: Leaders often feel a need to justify an earlier decision even after agreeing to replace it.
Over-explaining a change of plan wastes the team's time and is mostly for the leader's own benefit.
The habit connects to escalation of commitment, where effort keeps flowing to an inferior approach.
Committing to a plan does not mean defending it when a better option arrives.
The simple fix is to correct the heading and move forward without apology or lengthy justification.
quotes: Committing to a plan doesn’t mean we have to defend it when something better comes along, or a change of direction is needed.
The real trap is wasting too much time and effort defending and explaining our original position.
Here, we’ve agreed to change the plan, but apparently the old one still deserves a closing argument, whereas we could just call it what it is; wasting time.
You can see it’s better, but first you explain that you’d chosen email because everyone was familiar with it.
Next time I realise I’m heading in the wrong direction, whether that’s on a footpath or at work, I’m simply going to correct my heading and move forwards.
It’s okay to admit we got it wrong or that someone else has thought of a better way to do things.
